question: A 34-year-old man consulted for fever and malaise. In the clinical history, homosexual relationships were collected for 4 months with a new partner. 2 months before the current consultation, she had an ulcerous lesion on the glans, painless, with bilateral inguinal adenopathies, all self-limiting. Serological studies are requested with the following results: HIV negative, RPR 1/320, TPHA 1/128. What treatment would you indicate in this patient?

options.opb: Intravenous penicillin G, 24 MU every day for 14 days.
options.opc: Penicillin Benzatine 2.4 MU intramuscular, three doses in three consecutive weeks.
options.opd: Ceftriaxone 2 grams intramuscular in a single dose.
options.ope: Penicillin Benzatine 2.4 MU intramuscular in a single dose.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Primary syphilis infection -> ulcerous lesion on the glans -> painless -> bilateral inguinal adenopathies -> self-limiting -> RPR 1/320, TPHA 1/128 -> possible syphilis infection -> treatment decision required -> 80% confidence. CHAIN: Positive RPR 1/320, TPHA 1/128 -> indicative of syphilis infection -> treatment needed -> 90% confidence. CHAIN: Negative HIV result -> not related to the treatment decision -> 95% confidence. CHAIN: Treatment for syphilis infection -> Penicillin Benzathine 2.4 MU intramuscular in a single dose -> recommended first-line treatment -> 90% confidence. CHAIN: Penicillin Benzathine 2.4 MU intramuscular in a single dose -> effective for early syphilis -> 95% confidence. CHAIN: Penicillin Benzathine 2.4 MU intramuscular in a single dose -> preferred over other treatment options -> 80%
analysis: The patient's clinical history, symptoms, and serological results are suggestive of syphilis. The recommended treatment for early syphilis is Penicillin Benzathine 2.4 MU intramuscular in a single dose.
